panels.title: Offered load vs served
panels.description: If 'sent' > 'completed' the service is falling behind. Dropped iterations = k6 could not even start the request (all VUs stuck waiting).

panels.title: Client-side latency (k6)
panels.description: What the client actually experiences, including time queued in the TCP accept backlog.

panels.title: Server latency p50 / p95 / p99
panels.description: Measured inside Tomcat: excludes time a request spent waiting in the accept queue.

panels.title: Business operation time (incl. connection wait + commit)
Where does the time go? (avg per phase, confirmed orders)
panels.description: db-conn = waiting for a Hikari connection, lock = waiting for the inventory row lock. The phase that grows first under load is the bottleneck.

panels.title: Tomcat request threads
panels.description: busy == max -> every worker is occupied; new connections wait in the accept queue (accept-count) and then get refused.

panels.title: GC: time spent pausing
panels.description: Fraction of wall-clock time in GC pauses. Climbing towards 10%+ = memory pressure.

targets.expr: sum by (name) (rate(container_cpu_usage_seconds_total{name=~"$container"}[$__rate_interval])) / on (name) (max by (name) (container_spec_cpu_quota{name=~"$container"}) / max by (name) (container_spec_cpu_period{name=~"$container"}))

panels.title: CPU throttling
panels.description: Share of 100ms CFS periods in which the container wanted more CPU than its limit allowed.

panels.title: All containers — CPU cores used
panels.description: Is something else on the box (Prometheus, Loki, ...) stealing CPU?

panels.title: Hikari pool
panels.description: active == max and 'waiting threads' > 0 -> the pool is the bottleneck.

panels.title: Connection hold time (avg)
panels.description: How long each transaction keeps a connection. Pool capacity ≈ pool size / hold time.

panels.title: InnoDB row lock waits
panels.description: SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on inventory. Rises sharply with HOT_PRODUCTS.

panels.title: Orders — one line per request (CONFIRMED / REJECTED / FAILED)
